📌 Batch Auctions: Why Trades Can Work Better When Executed Together

Main Points
⏺ A batch auction collects many orders and executes them in one round
⏺ Participants receive a shared clearing price instead of random execution order
⏺ This post explains how the model can reduce damage from front-running

1️⃣ Core Idea — orders are not executed instantly one by one, but grouped into a batch.
2️⃣ Clearing Price — the system finds a price where the maximum amount of trading can happen.
3️⃣ Why It Helps — there is less room for someone to jump ahead of your trade and worsen your price.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — execution may not be instant, and results depend on liquidity inside the batch.
5️⃣ Practical Lens — batch auctions help when fair execution matters more than raw speed.

Final Thoughts

A batch auction turns trading from “who clicked first” into “who got a fair price.” Not magic, but a useful tool against order-flow chaos.

### 📉 The Compression Curve In Action

As a pool grows and matures, its yield naturally stabilizes. You can see this live curve playing out right now across GalaSwap’s 0.3% fee tier pools:

How much liquidity can the SOL/BTC pool actually hold before compressing to ordinary DeFi rates?

🔔 Zcash price holds above $1,200 as sell signal appears 

➡️ Zcash price traded near $1,216 on Sep. 10 after a seven-day rally of more than 50%, but overbought momentum, a three-day sell signal and nearby liquidation clusters raised the risk of a pullback. According to data from cryptonews, Zcash price was trading at $1,216.15 at the time of writing, down 2.26% for the session after opening at $1,244.18. The token traded between an intraday low of $1,204.93 and a high of $1,256.80.  

📊 Despite the daily decline, ZEC remained one of the strongest large-cap crypto performers over the past week. Its price rose more than 50% from around $814 on Sep. 4 and briefly entered the $1,249–$1,257 area before buyers lost momentum. The breakout also placed Zcash above $1,000 for the first time in years. Price continued to hold more than $200 above the psychological level at the time of writing, even as Bitcoin and Ethereum faced broader selling pressure.

⚡️ Derivatives liquidations contributed to the initial acceleration. More than $34.5 million in ZEC short positions were reportedly closed during a 24-hour period as bearish traders were forced to buy back the asset. Short liquidations accounted for about 94% of the total cited liquidations. Forced buying helped ZEC clear resistance quickly, but the same leverage that drove the advance could increase volatility if traders begin taking profits.

🚨 25 YEARS LATER: 9/11 QUESTIONS ARE BEING REDISCOVERED

Something very noticeable is happening around the 25th anniversary of September 11.

It isn’t simply that people are talking about 9/11 again. Major media outlets themselves are now reporting on the persistence, renewed circulation, and mainstream reach of 9/11 conspiracy theories—particularly as a new generation encounters the footage and arguments through modern social media.

Consider what is appearing almost simultaneously:

🔹 CNN: CNN’s extensive 25th-anniversary coverage illustrates just how much 9/11 has returned to the center of the media conversation, across television, streaming and digital platforms.

The larger generational shift matters: millions of Americans were either children on 9/11 or weren’t born yet. They are now encountering the event through an entirely different information ecosystem.

🔹 AL JAZEERA: “How 9/11 conspiracy theories moved into mainstream American politics.”

That’s an extraordinary framing by itself: “moved into mainstream.”

Al Jazeera describes how 9/11 theories migrated from the early Internet and films such as Loose Change into today’s much larger online ecosystem. It also examines how distrust following Iraq and the false WMD claims contributed to skepticism of government accounts. (Al Jazeera)

🔹 WIRED: “Conspiracy! How 9/11 Broke America’s Brain.”

WIRED devoted a major 25th-anniversary feature to the history of the 9/11 Truth movement—from radio and the early Internet through the enormous alternative-media ecosystem that followed. (WIRED)

🔹 DEUTSCHE WELLE: “9/11 conspiracy theories that continue to circulate.”

Twenty-five years later, another international news organization decided the continuing popularity of alternative explanations surrounding September 11 warranted its own anniversary story. (DW)

🔹 LEAD STORIES: “25 Years Later: The Top 9/11 Conspiracy Theory Fact Checks Readers Are Searching For.”

Notice the operative word:

SEARCHING.

The outlet assembled a special 25th-anniversary collection based on the 9/11 claims readers continue looking for information about—including the Pentagon and Osama bin Laden narratives. (Lead Stories)

🔹 SOCIAL MEDIA MONITORING: CyberWell reported finding scores of resurfacing 9/11-related conspiracy posts across Meta, Reddit, TikTok and X immediately ahead of the anniversary. Its analysis focused specifically on antisemitic variants, so it shouldn’t be treated as a measurement of the entire 9/11 Truth conversation—but it provides another independent indication that old 9/11 narratives are recirculating through today’s platforms. (CyberWell)

⚠️ THE PATTERN IS THE STORY.

Al Jazeera: “moved into mainstream”

Deutsche Welle: “continue to circulate”

CyberWell: “resurfacing”

Lead Stories: people are actively “searching”

And WIRED devotes an entire major feature to the cultural legacy of the 9/11 Truth movement.

Different organizations.

Different audiences.

Different perspectives.

But they’re all talking about essentially the same phenomenon at essentially the same time:

🔥 A NEW GENERATION IS REDISCOVERING 9/11.

And they’re discovering it very differently from the generation that lived through it.

Twenty years ago, someone questioning aspects of the official account might have needed to find a DVD, documentary, specialized website, message board or hours-long video.

Today?

Someone watches a 30-second Building 7 clip.

The algorithm serves another.

Then an old television report.

Then an interview.

Then a podcast.

Then another clip.

Then they start searching for themselves.

That’s an entirely different information environment.

Whether someone accepts the official account, questions portions of it, or believes alternative explanations is separate from the trend we’re documenting.

The observable phenomenon is that questions and conspiracy theories surrounding 9/11 are undergoing a very visible cultural resurgence around the 25th anniversary—and mainstream media is now openly discussing that resurgence itself.
